class V2AliasRouteTests(LiveServerTestCase):
    """The turn-3 V2 alias catalog is installed at server startup and is
    reachable, protected, and behaves exactly like its canonical V1 route.
    """

    def test_v2_record_then_v1_query_round_trip(self) -> None:
        status, body = self._request(
            "POST",
            "/v2/entries",
            body={"actor": "operator:mina", "action": "policy.update", "outcome": "allowed"},
            headers=self._auth(),
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 201)
        self.assertEqual(body["sequence"], 1)

        status, body = self._request("GET", "/v1/entries?actor=operator%3Amina", headers=self._auth())
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(len(body["entries"]), 1)

    def test_v1_record_then_v2_query_round_trip(self) -> None:
        status, _ = self._request(
            "POST",
            "/v1/entries",
            body={"actor": "operator:mina", "action": "policy.update", "outcome": "allowed"},
            headers=self._auth(),
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 201)

        status, body = self._request("GET", "/v2/entries", headers=self._auth())
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(len(body["entries"]), 1)

    def test_v2_integrity_route_reports_a_clean_store(self) -> None:
        status, body = self._request("GET", "/v2/integrity", headers=self._auth())
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["tampered"], [])

    def test_v2_route_without_a_bearer_is_rejected(self) -> None:
        status, _ = self._request("GET", "/v2/entries")
        self.assertEqual(status, 401)

    def test_v2_route_with_the_wrong_bearer_is_rejected(self) -> None:
        status, _ = self._request(
            "GET", "/v2/entries", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer wrong-token"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 401)

    def test_v2_route_ambiguous_percent_encoding_is_refused_before_auth(self) -> None:
        status, _ = self._request("GET", "/v2/entries%2F")
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)

    def test_v2_route_alternate_spelling_reaches_the_same_route(self) -> None:
        status, body = self._request("GET", "/v2//entries/", headers=self._auth())
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["entries"], [])

    def test_v1_route_is_unaffected_by_v2_installation(self) -> None:
        status, body = self._request("GET", "/v1/entries", headers=self._auth())
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["entries"], [])

    def test_unknown_v2_route_is_404(self) -> None:
        status, _ = self._request("GET", "/v2/nope", headers=self._auth())
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)

    def test_unknown_path_outside_both_catalogs_is_still_404(self) -> None:
        status, _ = self._request("GET", "/v3/entries", headers=self._auth())
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)

class V2AliasRouteTests(LiveServerTestCase):
    """The turn-3 V2 alias catalog is installed at server startup and is
    reachable, protected, and behaves exactly like its canonical V1 route.
    """

    def test_v2_record_then_v1_query_round_trip(self) -> None:
        status, body = self._request(
            "POST",
            "/v2/entries",
            body={"actor": "operator:mina", "action": "policy.update", "outcome": "allowed"},
            headers=self._auth(),
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 201)
        self.assertEqual(body["sequence"], 1)

        status, body = self._request("GET", "/v1/entries?actor=operator%3Amina", headers=self._auth())
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(len(body["entries"]), 1)

    def test_v1_record_then_v2_query_round_trip(self) -> None:
        status, _ = self._request(
            "POST",
            "/v1/entries",
            body={"actor": "operator:mina", "action": "policy.update", "outcome": "allowed"},
            headers=self._auth(),
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 201)

        status, body = self._request("GET", "/v2/entries", headers=self._auth())
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(len(body["entries"]), 1)

    def test_v2_integrity_route_reports_a_clean_store(self) -> None:
        status, body = self._request("GET", "/v2/integrity", headers=self._auth())
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["tampered"], [])

    def test_v2_route_without_a_bearer_is_rejected(self) -> None:
        status, _ = self._request("GET", "/v2/entries")
        self.assertEqual(status, 401)

    def test_v2_route_with_the_wrong_bearer_is_rejected(self) -> None:
        status, _ = self._request(
            "GET", "/v2/entries", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer wrong-token"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 401)

    def test_v2_route_ambiguous_percent_encoding_is_refused_before_auth(self) -> None:
        status, _ = self._request("GET", "/v2/entries%2F")
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)

    def test_v2_route_alternate_spelling_reaches_the_same_route(self) -> None:
        status, body = self._request("GET", "/v2//entries/", headers=self._auth())
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["entries"], [])

    def test_v1_route_is_unaffected_by_v2_installation(self) -> None:
        status, body = self._request("GET", "/v1/entries", headers=self._auth())
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["entries"], [])

    def test_unknown_v2_route_is_404(self) -> None:
        status, _ = self._request("GET", "/v2/nope", headers=self._auth())
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)

    def test_unknown_path_outside_both_catalogs_is_still_404(self) -> None:
        status, _ = self._request("GET", "/v3/entries", headers=self._auth())
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)

All 158 tests pass (148 previous + 10 new V2 alias tests), no regressions.

Summary of what changed in `auditlog/httpd.py`:

- `resolve_v2_alias_catalog` already existed with the exact required signature — unchanged; it already maps `None` to the matching V1 path (`path.replace("/v2/", "/v1/", 1)`) and requires that canonical key from `canonical_bearer`, defaulting to `True` (fail-secure) when absent.
- Added `_V1_ROUTES` (the three real V1 `(method, path) → permission` entries) and `_V1_BEARER_REQUIREMENTS` (all `True`, reflecting that every V1 route actually requires a bearer today) as the canonical table V2 aliases resolve against.
- `build_server` now calls `resolve_v2_alias_catalog(build_v2_alias_catalog(), _V1_BEARER_REQUIREMENTS)` at startup — the turn-3 catalog — and passes the resolved tuple into `make_handler`, which installs it alongside the V1 routes in a single `route_table` keyed by `(method, path)`, with V1 entries taking priority (`setdefault`) so V1 is never overridden.
- `_handle` now does exactly one path normalization (`auth_path`), then one route-table lookup that decides both the permission (record/query/integrity) and that specific route's own `requires_auth` — replacing the old unconditional bearer check with a per-route one. Paths not in the table (V1, V2, or anything else) still 404 unchanged.

Added `V2AliasRouteTests` to `tests/test_httpd.py` (10 real loopback tests against a live `build_server` instance): V2→V1 and V1→V2 round-trips for record/query, V2 integrity, missing/wrong bearer rejection on V2, ambiguous percent-encoding refused before auth on V2, alternate-spelling normalization reaching the same V2 route, V1 behavior unaffected, and 404 for unknown V2 and unrelated (`/v3/...`) paths.

"""Exercise the real, running loopback server (python -m auditlog.cli serve)
over actual HTTP, using urllib against 127.0.0.1:8790. Prints one line per
request: method, path, whether a bearer token was sent, HTTP status, body.
"""
import json
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:8790"
TOKEN = "gw-v2-integration-secret"


def call(method, path, use_bearer=None, body=None):
    headers = {}
    if use_bearer == "correct":
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {TOKEN}"
    elif use_bearer == "wrong":
        headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer wrong-token"
    data = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8") if body is not None else None
    if data is not None:
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"{BASE}{path}", data=data, method=method, headers=headers)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
            status = resp.status
            text = resp.read().decode("utf-8")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        status = exc.code
        text = exc.read().decode("utf-8")
    bearer_desc = {"correct": "valid bearer", "wrong": "wrong bearer", None: "no bearer"}[use_bearer]
    print(f"{method} {path}  [{bearer_desc}]  -> {status}  {text}")
    return status, text

# Gateway V2 Integration: Live Loopback Verification

This document records a real run of the audit log server through its
documented CLI entry point, followed by real HTTP requests against it over
`127.0.0.1`, proving the installed V2 aliases (`auditlog/httpd.py`,
`auditlog/policy.py`) behave as designed against a live process rather than
only under `unittest`. No test code or application code was modified to
produce this record; it is an exercise of the shipped server as-is.

## 1. Server startup

Command actually run (background process; log store and bearer token are
this run's own throwaway values, port is caller-selected):

```
python -m auditlog.cli serve \
  --log-store gateway-v2-store.sqlite3 \
  --bearer-token gw-v2-integration-secret \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8790
```

Readiness probe (real HTTP `GET /v1/entries` with the correct bearer),
confirming the process was up and serving before any exercise began:

```
python -c "import urllib.request; r = urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request('http://127.0.0.1:8790/v1/entries', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer gw-v2-integration-secret'})); print(r.status, r.read())"
```

Result:

```
200 b'{"entries": []}'
```

The server was later stopped cleanly (`TaskStop` on the background process)
once every exercise below had run.

## 2. How every request below was sent

Each request in Sections A–D was sent with Python's `urllib.request` against
the running process at `http://127.0.0.1:8790`, driven by a small script
(`exercise_v2.py`) making one real HTTP call per line — no mocking, no
in-process test client. Each line documents the exact method, path, whether
a bearer token was attached (and which one), and the real response the
server sent back.

## 3. Section A — the supplied gateway compatibility cases

Source: `fixtures/gateway-compatibility-cases.json`, exercised verbatim
against the live server (`canonical-record` implies `POST` given its
`201 Created` expectation; `missing-token` is the same request with the
`Authorization` header withheld):

| case | request | expected_status | actual status | actual body |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `canonical-record` | `POST /v2/entries` with valid bearer | 201 | **201** | `{"event_id": "098f3083...", "sequence": 1, "actor": "operator:mina", "action": "policy.update", "outcome": "allowed", "recorded_at": "2026-08-31T19:15:59Z", "metadata": {}}` |
| `missing-token` | `POST /v2/entries` with no bearer | 401 | **401** | `{"error": "bearer token required"}` |

Both fixture cases matched their `expected_status` exactly.

## 4. Section B — authenticated V2 requests through normalized spellings

Every request below carried a valid `Authorization: Bearer
gw-v2-integration-secret` header. Each spelling variant (repeated slash,
trailing slash, printable-ASCII percent-encoding) normalizes to the same
canonical path as the documented spelling per `auditlog/paths.py`, and each
reached the same route with the same result:

| request sent | status | body |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v2/entries` | 200 | *(201, see below)* |

# Gateway V2 Integration: Live Loopback Verification

This document records a real run of the audit log server through its
documented CLI entry point, followed by real HTTP requests against it over
`127.0.0.1`, proving the installed V2 aliases (`auditlog/httpd.py`,
`auditlog/policy.py`) behave as designed against a live process rather than
only under `unittest`. No test code or application code was modified to
produce this record; it is an exercise of the shipped server as-is.

## 1. Server startup

Command actually run (background process; log store and bearer token are
this run's own throwaway values, port is caller-selected):

```
python -m auditlog.cli serve \
  --log-store gateway-v2-store.sqlite3 \
  --bearer-token gw-v2-integration-secret \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8790
```

Readiness probe (real HTTP `GET /v1/entries` with the correct bearer),
confirming the process was up and serving before any exercise began:

```
python -c "import urllib.request; r = urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request('http://127.0.0.1:8790/v1/entries', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer gw-v2-integration-secret'})); print(r.status, r.read())"
```

Result:

```
200 b'{"entries": []}'
```

The server was later stopped cleanly (`TaskStop` on the background process)
once every exercise below had run.

## 2. How every request below was sent

Each request in Sections A–D was sent with Python's `urllib.request` against
the running process at `http://127.0.0.1:8790`, driven by a small script
(`exercise_v2.py`) making one real HTTP call per line — no mocking, no
in-process test client. Each line documents the exact method, path, whether
a bearer token was attached (and which one), and the real response the
server sent back.

## 3. Section A — the supplied gateway compatibility cases

Source: `fixtures/gateway-compatibility-cases.json`, exercised verbatim
against the live server (`canonical-record` implies `POST` given its
`201 Created` expectation; `missing-token` is the same request with the
`Authorization` header withheld):

| case | request | expected_status | actual status | actual body |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `canonical-record` | `POST /v2/entries` with valid bearer | 201 | **201** | `{"event_id": "098f3083...", "sequence": 1, "actor": "operator:mina", "action": "policy.update", "outcome": "allowed", "recorded_at": "2026-08-31T19:15:59Z", "metadata": {}}` |
| `missing-token` | `POST /v2/entries` with no bearer | 401 | **401** | `{"error": "bearer token required"}` |

Both fixture cases matched their `expected_status` exactly.

## 4. Section B — authenticated V2 requests through normalized spellings

Every request below carried a valid `Authorization: Bearer
gw-v2-integration-secret` header. Each spelling variant (repeated slash,
trailing slash, printable-ASCII percent-encoding) normalizes to the same
canonical path as the documented spelling per `auditlog/paths.py`, and each
reached the same route with the same result:

| request sent | status | body |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v2/entries` (canonical) | **201** | `{"event_id": "b5bd6f99...", "sequence": 2, "actor": "svc:gateway", ...}` |
| `POST /v2//entries` (repeated slash) | **201** | `{"event_id": "b5bd6f99...", "sequence": 3, "actor": "svc:gateway", ...}` |
| `POST /v2/%65ntries` (percent-encoded `e`) | **201** | `{"event_id": "b5bd6f99...", "sequence": 4, "actor": "svc:gateway", ...}` |
| `GET /v2/entries` (canonical) | **200** | 4 entries returned |
| `GET /v2/entries/` (trailing slash) | **200** | same 4 entries returned |
| `GET /v2//entries` (repeated slash) | **200** | same 4 entries returned |
| `GET /v2/%65ntries` (percent-encoded `e`) | **200** | same 4 entries returned |
| `GET /v2/integrity` (canonical) | **200** | `{"verified": 4, "tampered": [], "migrated": false, "index_rebuilt": true}` |
| `GET /v2/integrity/` (trailing slash) | **200** | identical report |
| `GET /v2//integrity` (repeated slash) | **200** | identical report |
| `GET /v2/%69ntegrity` (percent-encoded `i`) | **200** | identical report |

Every normalized spelling of `POST /v2/entries`, `GET /v2/entries`, and
`GET /v2/integrity` reached the exact same route as its canonical spelling,
with a valid bearer accepted every time.

Note: the three `POST /v2/entries` calls in this section all carry
identical `(actor, action, outcome, recorded_at)` content (they ran within
the same wall-clock second), so they share one content-derived `event_id`
(`b5bd6f99...`) while still occupying three distinct, gapless sequence
numbers (2, 3, 4) — expected behavior of `AuditService.record`, which
always appends; content-based deduplication is a separate, opt-in concern
(`auditlog/replay.py`), not something the plain record path performs.

## 5. Section C — the same requests fail without a bearer token

Same routes as Section B, now with no `Authorization` header (or the wrong
one):

| request sent | bearer | status | body |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /v2/entries` | none | **401** | `{"error": "bearer token required"}` |
| `GET /v2/entries` | none | **401** | `{"error": "bearer token required"}` |
| `GET /v2/integrity` | none | **401** | `{"error": "bearer token required"}` |
| `GET /v2/entries` | wrong token | **401** | `{"error": "bearer token required"}` |

Every V2 route that succeeded with a valid bearer in Section B failed with
`401` when the bearer was missing or wrong — the resolved `requires_auth`
for every turn-3 V2 alias is `True`, and the live server enforces it.

## 6. Section D — ambiguous paths remain rejected

| request sent | bearer | status | body |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /v2/entries%2F` | none | **400** | `{"error": "percent-encoding is ambiguous: %2F"}` |
| `GET /v2/entries%2F` | valid | **400** | `{"error": "percent-encoding is ambiguous: %2F"}` |
| `GET /v2/entries%00` | valid | **400** | `{"error": "percent-encoding decodes to a control character: %00"}` |
| `GET /v2/entries%zz` | valid | **400** | `{"error": "malformed percent-encoding: '%zz'"}` |
| `GET /v2/integrity%2F` | valid | **400** | `{"error": "percent-encoding is ambiguous: %2F"}` |

A percent-encoded `/`, a percent-encoded control byte, and a malformed
percent sequence are all refused with `400` on a real V2 request, and the
refusal happens identically with or without a valid bearer present —
confirming path normalization is rejected before the bearer check runs, on
the live server, not just in `unittest`.

## Summary

Every exercise against the real, running `python -m auditlog.cli serve`
process matched what `tests/test_httpd.py::V2AliasRouteTests` already
asserts under `unittest`: the turn-3 V2 alias catalog is installed at
startup, reachable under every bounded normalized spelling, gated by its
own resolved bearer requirement, and paths outside the bounded
normalization set are refused with `400` before that bearer check ever
runs. No product code was changed to produce this record.

# Post-Cutover Gateway Runbook: V1/V2 Handoff

This is a documentation-only handoff. Nothing in `auditlog/` was changed to
produce it — every example below is a real, reproduced call into the
already-shipped normalizer (`auditlog/paths.py`) or the already-shipped
route table (`auditlog/httpd.py`, `auditlog/policy.py`), and every outcome
in §4 is a real `unittest` run against the unmodified suite. Route behavior
is exactly what it was before this document was written.

## 1. Supported normalization

`auditlog/paths.py::canonical_path` resolves exactly three bounded
compatibility spellings, and refuses everything else outright rather than
guessing (see §3). `auth_path` and `dispatch_path` both call it, and the
server calls it exactly once per request (`auditlog/httpd.py::_handle`), so
the route decision and the handler invocation always agree on the same
spelling.

| Supported spelling | Example | Normalizes to |
|---|---|---|
| Repeated slashes collapse to one | `/v2//entries` | `/v2/entries` |
| One trailing slash is dropped | `/v2/entries/` | `/v2/entries` |
| A percent-encoded printable-ASCII byte decodes | `/v2/%65ntries` | `/v2/entries` |

Verified directly against the shipped normalizer:

```
python -c "from auditlog.paths import canonical_path as c; print(c('/v2//entries'), c('/v2/entries/'), c('/v2/%65ntries'))"
```

```
/v2/entries /v2/entries /v2/entries
```

All three spellings resolve to the identical canonical path, so a request
sent through any of them reaches the same route with the same
authorization requirement — this was re-verified live against a running
server in `docs/gateway-v2-integration.md` §4.

## 2. Route behavior (unchanged by this document)

Installed at server startup by `build_server()` (`auditlog/httpd.py`):
three V1 routes, unconditionally, plus the turn-3 V2 alias catalog
(`auditlog/policy.py::build_v2_alias_catalog`) resolved through
`resolve_v2_alias_catalog` against the real V1 bearer table.

| Method | Path | Permission | Requires auth |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/v1/entries` | record | True |
| GET | `/v1/entries` | query | True |
| GET | `/v1/integrity` | integrity | True |
| POST | `/v2/entries` | record | True |
| GET | `/v2/entries` | query | True |
| GET | `/v2/integrity` | integrity | True |

Nothing in this table changed as part of this handoff. Any path not in it
— including a `/v3/...` path or an unrecognized `/v1/...`/`/v2/...` path —
still 404s.

## 3. Refusal examples

Every refusal below comes from `auditlog/paths.py::canonical_path`, is
raised before the bearer check ever runs, and was reproduced directly:

```
python -c "
from auditlog.paths import canonical_path, PathNormalizationError
for path in ['/v2/entries%2F', '/v2/entries%25', '/v2/entries%00', '/v2/entries%C3', '/v2/entries%zz', '/v2/entries%6']:
    try:
        canonical_path(path)
    except PathNormalizationError as e:
        print(path, '->', e)
"
```

| Path sent | Why it's refused | Status | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/v2/entries%2F` | percent-encoded `/` would change which segment the path resolves to | 400 | `percent-encoding is ambiguous: %2F` |
| `/v2/entries%25` | percent-encoded `%` is the same ambiguity in the other direction | 400 | `percent-encoding is ambiguous: %25` |
| `/v2/entries%00` | decodes to a control byte | 400 | `percent-encoding decodes to a control character: %00` |
| `/v2/entries%C3` | decodes outside the bounded printable-ASCII range | 400 | `percent-encoding outside the bounded ASCII range: %C3` |
| `/v2/entries%zz` | not a valid hex pair | 400 | `malformed percent-encoding: '%zz'` |
| `/v2/entries%6` | truncated hex pair | 400 | `malformed percent-encoding: '%6'` |
| a raw control character in the path | never percent-encoded at all | 400 | `path contains a raw control character: ...` |

A missing or wrong bearer on an otherwise well-formed, normalized path is
refused separately, at 401, only after the path clears normalization —
`{"error": "bearer token required"}`. Both refusal classes were reproduced
live against a running server in `docs/gateway-v2-integration.md` §5–§6.

## 4. Rollback steps

This codebase has no runtime toggle for the V2 catalog — `build_server()`
always resolves and installs it. Rollback is therefore always one of the
following, depending on what actually needs undoing:

1. **Stop advertising `/v2/*` upstream.** V1 routes are installed
   unconditionally and never depend on whether V2 is reachable
   (`_V1_ROUTES` / `_V1_BEARER_REQUIREMENTS` in `auditlog/httpd.py`), so
   the only lever for "turn V2 back off" is at the gateway/reverse-proxy
   tier in front of this loopback service: stop forwarding `/v2/*`
   upstream. No V1 client is ever affected either way.
2. **Never roll back a recorded event.** `AuditEvent` is a frozen
   dataclass and the store is append-only, with `AuditService.record`
   enforcing a gapless sequence (`_verify_sequence`). There is no
   "undo a recorded event" step in any cutover, planned or emergency —
   correcting a mistaken entry means recording a new, corrective event,
   never rewriting or deleting the old one.
3. **Resume, don't roll back, an interrupted gateway import batch.** If a
   batch through `auditlog/replay.py::import_gateway_requests` was cut off
   mid-cutover (crash, restart, network interruption), rerun the same
   batch against the same store and ledger files. Restart-safety is
   designed in: a request already completed replays as a no-op
   (`replayed=True`); a request that was pending but never appended
   finishes exactly once; nothing is ever double-appended, and a
   request that resolves to a *different* path or content than its first
   import is rejected as a conflict (`ReplayConflictError`) rather than
   silently applied. Re-verified in §5 below.
4. **File-level store rollback is operational, not a code feature.** The
   on-disk SQLite log-store and replay-ledger files are ordinary files.
   If a pre-cutover point-in-time backup exists, restoring it is: stop the
   server, replace the store/ledger files with the backup copies, restart.
   This document does not assert such a backup exists for any particular
   deployment — only that the file format supports this if one was taken.

## 5. Test suite outcomes

All four suites below ran against the unmodified codebase (`python`
resolved from `PATH`, `unittest discover`, no code edits before, during,
or after). Every run reported `OK`.

### V1/V2 gateway suite — `tests/test_httpd.py`

```
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_httpd.py" -v
```

```
Ran 40 tests in 6.604s

OK
```

Covers loopback host refusal, SQLite persistence, bearer auth, malformed
gateway-envelope handling, ambiguous-path refusal, the three V1 routes,
and the six installed V2 alias routes (`V2AliasRouteTests`).

### Authorization suite — `tests/test_gateway_policy.py`

```
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_gateway_policy.py" -v
```

```
Ran 7 tests in 0.000s

OK
```

Covers `resolve_v2_alias_catalog`: explicit `True`/`False` passes through
untouched, an inherited (`None`) entry takes its canonical V1 route's
requirement, an inherited entry with no canonical route defaults to
requiring auth, the published turn-3 catalog requires auth everywhere, and
path normalization never changes which catalog entry answers a request.

### Replay suite — `tests/test_replay.py`

```
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_replay.py" -v
```

```
Ran 20 tests in 2.057s

OK
```

Covers fresh imports, duplicate envelopes (same request replayed, a
duplicate within one batch, two different request ids with identical
content), conflicts (differing path, differing content, a rejected
conflict leaving store and ledger unchanged), normalization stability,
crash recovery, separate-process continuation, event immutability, and
that a bearer token is never persisted to either the ledger or the store
file.

### Restart suite — `tests/test_replay.py::CrashRecoveryTests` + `SeparateProcessContinuationTests`

```
python -m unittest discover -s tests -k CrashRecoveryTests -k SeparateProcessContinuationTests -v
```

```
test_append_already_landed_before_the_crash_is_not_repeated ... ok
test_pending_with_no_append_yet_completes_exactly_once_on_retry ... ok
test_sequence_order_survives_a_crash_partway_through_a_batch ... ok
test_a_fresh_store_and_ledger_pair_resumes_correctly ... ok

Ran 4 tests in 0.411s

OK
```

Directly exercises the rollback story in §4.3: a pending-but-unappended
request completes exactly once on retry; an appended-but-not-yet-marked
request is not repeated; sequence order survives a crash partway through a
batch; and a completely fresh `AuditService`/`SqliteLogStore`/
`SqliteReplayLedger` triple sharing the same on-disk files resumes
correctly, simulating a real process restart.

### Full regression — every test in `tests/`

```
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

```
Ran 158 tests in 13.066s

OK
```

Per-module breakdown: `test_cli_serve` 6, `test_compat_report` 15,
`test_gateway_envelope` 9, `test_gateway_policy` 7, `test_httpd` 40,
`test_models` 11, `test_paths` 26, `test_policy` 3, `test_replay` 20,
`test_service` 17, `test_starter` 4 — sums to 158, matching the reported
total. Nothing outside the four suites above regressed.

## Handoff note

Route behavior is unchanged: no file under `auditlog/` was edited to
produce this runbook. Every normalization example, refusal example, and
test-suite outcome above was reproduced directly against the code as it
stands today, not asserted from memory or an earlier turn.
